analysis: Purkinje cells in the cerebellum receive direct input from climbing fibers. Climbing fibers originate from the inferior olivary nucleus in the medulla and form powerful excitatory synapses on Purkinje cells. While mossy fibers also play a role in cerebellar input, they do not directly synapse on Purkinje cells; instead, they synapse on granule cells, which then influence Purkinje cells via parallel fibers.
